clue.text: Local government advice for auditors

indicators.note: auditors are listeners, so the word for advice is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: counsel is guidance or advice given

explanation.surface: A council offering guidance to the accountants who check its books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' looks like accountants; here it means hearers, so COUNSEL said out loud gives the spelling for the local body.
explanation.definitionFit: A town or county body elected to run local affairs is the standard unit of local administration.

clue.text: Stall and hit rocks left nearer the bottom

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so the letter for left is shifted towards it

parts.note: to club is to hit with a cudgel
rocks is slang for ice, as in whisky on the rocks

explanation.surface: A stallholder hits some rocks with the leftovers dumped nearer the floor.
explanation.walkthrough: CLUB+ICE gives CLUBICE; moving L down the grid gives CUBICLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A stall is a small compartment such as a toilet cubicle or one in a stable.

clue.text: After articles in three countries a man flees abroad incognito

indicators.note: the rearranged part comes after the articles in the answer

parts.note: UN (French), DER (German) and A (English) are articles in three countries

indicators.note: abroad means scattered widely, so the letters are scattered

explanation.surface: Following articles in a few countries, a man flees overseas travelling unrecognised.
explanation.walkthrough: The three articles UN, DER, A then FALSENAME, the anagram of A MAN FLEES.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling incognito means concealing one's real identity, usually by using a pseudonym.

clue.text: 150 identical tips for festival

parts.note: C and L are Roman 100 and 50, read as C and L

indicators.note: to tip something is to tip it over, so the word is read upside down in a down clue

parts.note: identical means the same

explanation.surface: One hundred and fifty identical gratuities for a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 150 is C and L in Roman numerals, written C AND L; 'tips' turns SAME over to EMAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Candlemas is the Christian feast of 2 February marking the presentation of Jesus at the Temple.

clue.text: Watch bottom with round bits protruding

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or watch
the bed of a river or sea is its bottom

explanation.surface: Telling someone to look at a rear with bulging lumps.
explanation.walkthrough: LO is the archaic 'look', and BED the bottom of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A lobed leaf or ear has rounded projections, the meaning of the adjective.

clue.text: Jack, our lad, comes round to stay

indicators.note: the boy's word surrounds the other pieces, as if walking round them

parts.note: a lad is a boy or son
J is the card abbreviation for jack

explanation.surface: A young man named Jack visits to spend some time with us.
explanation.walkthrough: The son goes round J and OUR, giving SO-JOUR-N.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary stay somewhere, or to stay for a while, is a literary synonym.

clue.text: Girlfriend cut sandwiches and cried

indicators.note: the word for cut takes the girlfriend between its letters, like a sandwich filling

parts.note: to shear is to cut
a date is a romantic partner

explanation.surface: A girlfriend slicing bread for sandwiches sheds a tear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' looks like food but is the container signal; the answer reads as the phrase SHE'D A TEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Shedding a tear means weeping, so one who has done so has wept.

clue.text: GI (Republican) palms king and another card

indicators.note: to palm something is to hide it in the hand, so the soldier holds the king inside

parts.note: GI Joe is a US soldier
K is the abbreviation for king in cards and chess
R is the US abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A Republican American soldier hides a king and another card, cheating at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another card' refers back to the king: the joker is a further card.
explanation.definitionFit: A joker is an extra card in a standard pack, beyond the king and the rest.

clue.text: Goad communicant after Reformation, unlike 9 and 22

indicators.note: reformation is a re-forming, so the letters are made over into a new shape

explanation.surface: Urging a churchgoer after the Reformation to be different.
explanation.walkthrough: 9 and 22 are BED AND BREAKFAST and BOARD AND LODGING: both house guests, so their opposite is unwelcoming.
explanation.definitionFit: Both cross-referenced answers are places offering room and food, so something not offering them is unhelpful.

clue.text: Types behind keeping guard regularly

indicators.note: the buttocks word keeps the letters inside

parts.note: nates is the anatomical term for buttocks

indicators.note: regularly means alternate letters of guard

explanation.surface: Kinds of people lag behind and keep guard steadily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' looks like a preposition; it is the buttocks, NATES, holding UR from guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's nature is their kind or character, so natures are sorts or kinds.

clue.text: Briefly books guest house

parts.note: B is short for book, so books written briefly are B B, the familiar shorthand B and B for this kind of lodging

explanation.surface: A short instruction to reserve a room at a small hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly books' reads as 'quickly reserves', but B is the abbreviation for book, so books in short are B and B, the usual short form of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A small establishment offering a room for the night plus a morning meal is exactly a guest house.

clue.text: Pink radical wearing black stuff

indicators.note: the black stuff has the radical on it like a garment, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: coal is the black fuel dug from mines
R is an abbreviation for radical

explanation.surface: A left-wing militant in pink clothing over black gear.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes into COAL, giving CO-R-AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coral names a pinkish-orange shade, after the colour of the sea organism's skeleton.

clue.text: He puts his foot down: "Haul tree across river!"

indicators.note: the tree is laid across the river, lying beside it in the order of the answer

parts.note: to drag is to haul or pull
R is the map abbreviation for river
acer is the maple genus

explanation.surface: A forester's shout to pull a felled trunk over a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He puts his foot down' is a firm person; here it is a driver flooring the accelerator.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone racing short sprints on a straight track floors the accelerator pedal throughout, a playful description.

clue.text: Nice girl follows directions, hosting morning with her kin

indicators.note: the girl comes after the compass points in the answer

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north

indicators.note: the girl takes in the morning as a host takes a guest

parts.note: in Nice, France, a girl is une fille
AM is the abbreviation for the morning hours

explanation.surface: A young woman from Nice following directions with the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' is the French city, so the girl is French: FILLE, holding AM.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means at home with one's family, and the girl in the clue makes it her relatives.

clue.text: Given the runaround, English father boards cutter

indicators.note: to board is to get on, so the English father goes into the cutter

parts.note: a lance is a surgical knife for cutting
dad is father

explanation.surface: An English father boards a small boat and is led on a chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cutter' looks like a boat; it is the surgical LANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Led someone a dance means caused them trouble, giving them the runaround.

clue.text: Weeds cover front of most houses

indicators.note: the weeding word goes around the letter as a lid covers a pot

parts.note: to weed with a hoe: he hoes, he weeds

indicators.note: front means the first letter of the word most

explanation.surface: Overgrown plants hiding the facades of most dwellings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weeds' looks like a noun; it is the verb, giving HOES around M.
explanation.definitionFit: Houses are dwellings where people live, synonymous with residences.

clue.text: Estates in Spain misled, when recruiting 100 there

indicators.note: the deceit takes in the number like an army taking on recruits

parts.note: to have someone is to fool or mislead them
cien is one hundred in Spain's language
as can mean when

explanation.surface: Spanish estate agents who misled people while hiring a hundred staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'there' points back to Spain: CIEN is Spanish for 100; HAD (misled) takes it in, then AS.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large ranch or landed estate in Spain or Latin America.

clue.text: They're often barred in reception areas

definitions.text: They're often barred in reception areas

parts.words: They're often barred in reception areas
parts.note: prison rooms for new arrivals have bars on the window, and the zones served by a mobile mast show bars of signal

explanation.surface: Office foyers that are frequently locked off.
explanation.walkthrough: Reception is both receiving prisoners and mobile signal; a phone's zones are measured in bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Prison rooms are barred, and mobile coverage zones show signal bars, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Competent party boss apparently taken in

indicators.note: the party leader takes the short word in

parts.note: Vince Cable led the Liberal Democrats when the puzzle appeared
AP serves as a short form of apparently

explanation.surface: An able party leader is seemingly fooled.
explanation.walkthrough: Vince Cable was leader of the UK Liberal Democrats in 2018; AP for apparently is a loose abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable describes someone able and competent to do a task.

clue.text: Board day is inspiring cleric

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the two letters draw the cleric inside

parts.note: a rector is a parish priest

explanation.surface: A dull day enlivened by a motivating vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: IS takes RECTOR into its middle: D-I-RECTOR-S.
explanation.definitionFit: A company's board is the body of its governing members, so the plural fits as a collective.

clue.text: Cunning, extremely skilful rowers

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: an eight is a rowing crew of eight oarsmen

explanation.surface: Clever, highly skilled oarsmen.
explanation.walkthrough: SL, the ends of skilful, plus EIGHT, the crew.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight is dexterity or cunning, as in sleight of hand.

clue.text: CD and EP ruled out? Yes

definitions.text: CD and EP ruled out? Yes

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are in disorder, put out of place

explanation.surface: Asking whether two music formats have been banned, and confirming it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of CD, EP and RULED rearrange to the answer, and 'ruled out' is also what it means, hence the 'Yes'.
explanation.definitionFit: To preclude something is to prevent or exclude it in advance, so a format banned outright has been excluded.

clue.text: Austen girl fills in weekly diary

indicators.note: the girl fills a space inside the words, sitting within them

explanation.surface: A girl from an Austen novel completes her weekly journal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fills in' looks like writing; it means the name sits within the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Lydia Bennet is the youngest sister in Pride and Prejudice by the novelist Jane Austen.

clue.text: Penniless Greek city, one in Asia

indicators.note: without a penny, the abbreviation P is taken out

parts.note: Delphi is the ancient Greek city of the oracle

explanation.surface: A broke Greek town that is in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: P is the British abbreviation for a penny; 'one' stands for a city, as 'Greek city' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi is a major Indian city, so it is a city in Asia.

clue.text: Sidestep first woman clasping her mate? Not half

indicators.note: Eve holds the shortened partner in her arms, so he goes inside her

parts.note: Eve, in Genesis, is the first woman

indicators.note: only half of the partner's name is kept, the latter half dropped

parts.note: Eve's partner in Eden is Adam

explanation.surface: Avoiding Eve as she embraces her partner, or half of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also British slang for 'certainly!', but here it keeps only the first two letters of the partner's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to avoid or dodge, just as one steps aside from a blow.

clue.text: Male badger, escaping over ploughed land, digs

parts.note: a male badger is called a boar

indicators.note: the evasive word reaches over the turned soil, enclosing it

parts.note: dodging is evading or escaping

indicators.note: ploughed earth is turned over, so the letters are churned

explanation.surface: A badger fleeing across a farmer's freshly turned field and burrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badger' wants to be the verb 'pester'; it pairs with 'Male' as BOAR. 'Digs' is British slang for rented lodgings.
explanation.definitionFit: Digs is informal British for lodgings, a rented room usually with meals included.

clue.text: Put up European tax shelter limits

indicators.note: the shelter word forms the boundaries around the tax

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
VAT is value added tax, the UK sales tax

explanation.surface: European duty sets limits on tax havens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tax shelter' looks like one financial idea; the words split, and 'limits' says the shelter forms the borders of the tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To put up something is to raise it, as one would lift it higher.

clue.text: Understanding one thing's problematic

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: a problematic arrangement is a troubled one, so the letters are muddled

explanation.surface: Grasping one item is proving difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: THINGS (from thing's) is rearranged after I.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep perception or grasp of a situation, a synonym for comprehension.
